issues.claim: Rite-Hite states roughly 25% of warehouse injuries occur at or near the loading dock, attributing the figure to OSHA/NSC (problem.evidence[6]).
issues.problem: Misstated on three counts. The Rite-Hite page actually says 'The National Safety Council estimates ... that up to 25% of all industrial accidents occur at the loading dock.' (a) 'up to 25%' became 'roughly 25%'; (b) 'all industrial accidents' became 'warehouse injuries'; (c) the figure is attributed to NSC only, not OSHA/NSC. The caveat at the end of the brief half-concedes this, but the evidence entry itself, which an orchestrator may quote, overstates the number and its scope.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: 'Rite-Hite (vendor blog), citing NSC, estimates that up to 25% of all industrial accidents occur at the loading dock (no primary OSHA/NSC publication located).' Keep the vendor and 'up to' qualifiers in the fact string itself, not only in caveats.

issues.claim: Ailytics claims 60-80% reduction in safety non-compliance across 400+ projects and 6,000+ cameras (measured_outcomes[2]).
issues.problem: The cited page (ailytics.ai/industries/logistics-and-warehousing) states '400+ projects worldwide', '60-80% reduction in safety non-compliance' and '<2 weeks', but contains no '6,000+ cameras' figure anywhere on the page. The camera count appears on Ailytics' company LinkedIn, not on the cited URL.
issues.fix: Drop '6,000+ cameras', or re-cite to a page that actually states it (e.g. the Ailytics projects page or company LinkedIn) and label it company-reported.

issues.claim: '$11.5B lost productivity' from driver detention (problem.evidence[5] and measured_outcomes[6]).
issues.problem: ATRI reports $3.6 billion in unreimbursed direct expenses and, separately, $11.5 billion in lost revenue to the for-hire trucking industry ('lost as much as $11.5 billion in revenue due to detention in 2023'), with 135.9 million hours lost. Calling the $11.5B 'lost productivity' is a mislabel of the study's own category.
issues.fix: Change to '$3.6B in unreimbursed direct expenses plus $11.5B in lost revenue (135.9M driver hours)'. All other ATRI numbers (39.3% of stops, 117.5-209.4 hours per driver) are correct as written.

issues.claim: Americold attributed a ~70% reduction in injuries, with lost-time days falling from 288 to zero and $1.1M annual savings, at one cold-storage facility (measured_outcomes[1]).
issues.problem: Partly supported. The 288-to-zero days and $1.1M savings are in the body of the Voxel page, but the body credits 'up to 90% reduction in unsafe behaviors' and does not state a 70% injury reduction. The 70% appears only in the page headline/URL slug ('Reduced Injures By 70%'). The page also says losses were 'at several of its distribution centers', so 'one facility' is the author's framing, not the source's.
issues.fix: Restate as: 'Voxel case study headline claims a 70% injury reduction; body text reports up to 90% reduction in unsafe behaviours, zero days missed (down from 288) and $1.1M annual savings; site count not specified.' Keep strength Low.

issues.claim: fit_score: legal_risk_low = 11 of 20, while the rationale says 'Legal risk is moderate-low'.
issues.problem: Sub-scores do sum correctly (17+14+10+15+11+8 = 75) and sit in plausible ranges, but 11/20 is a middling score that does not match the 'moderate-low' characterisation. The legal section itself documents real residual risk (wiretap exposure on audio, a retraining duty created by the near-miss log, Section 7 surveillance objections), all of which are avoidable by design.
issues.fix: Either raise legal_risk_low to ~14-15 and keep the 'moderate-low' rationale, or keep 11 and restate the rationale as 'moderate, managed by design constraints' (video only, no biometrics, no discipline automation).

issues.claim: N.J.S.A. 2A:156A-4(d) cited as the one-party-consent provision.
issues.problem: The cited RCFP page supports the rule (one party's consent suffices; N.J. Stat. Ann. sections 2A:156A-2, -3, -4) and the criminal penalties, but it does not pin the rule to subsection (d). That subsection letter is unverified.
issues.fix: Cite the section generally (N.J.S.A. 2A:156A-4) unless a primary copy of the statute confirming subsection (d) is opened.

29 CFR 1910.178(k)(1) requires brakes set and wheel chocks under rear wheels while a highway truck is boarded with a PIT; (m)(7) requires brakes set and wheel blocks in place while loading/unloading.

1910.178(n)(1) requires approximately three truck lengths of following distance; (n)(4) requires slowing and sounding the horn at cross aisles and where vision is obstructed.
1910.37(a)(3): exit routes must be free and unobstructed, no materials or equipment placed in them.
1910.176(a): aisles and passageways kept clear, permanent aisles and passageways appropriately marked.
1904.39: fatality reportable within 8 hours; in-patient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye within 24 hours.

Friedman v. Martinez (N.J. 2020) recognised intrusion upon seclusion for hidden cameras in restrooms and allowed claims without proof images were actually captured.
